violated_invariant: A DVM pool's init() must only be callable once, so its token pair and maintainer cannot be replaced after deployment.
rationale: Inside DVMFlashLoanCall the PoC calls dvm.init() again on a live pool and swaps the base/quote tokens for attacker tokens, so the flash-loan repayment check runs against the fake tokens and the real wCRES/USDT are kept. The DVM (0x051ebd...) has no recovered source, so the function names come from the PoC interface. None of the candidates with source (wCRES token, a maintainer proxy, FeeRateModel) holds the defect, and the DHL label 'Flashloan Attack' names the mechanism, not the root cause.

violated_invariant: Only the deploying pool may initialize the NFT contract and become its owner; init() must not be callable by anyone afterwards.
rationale: The PoC comment and code show a public init() with no caller restriction that hands ownership to msg.sender; the attacker then burns and re-mints deposit NFT #1 to themselves. No source was recovered for 0xf0b7..., so the file and function names are guesses taken from the PoC. Impact is set to 'other' (deposit-NFT ownership hijack) and in_scope is low-certainty, because I could not confirm a realized USD loss. The DHL label 'Access control' is a fair parent, but unprotected init is the more specific root cause.

violated_invariant: Cross-chain messages relayed by EthCrossChainManager must never be able to call privileged functions on EthCrossChainData, which owns the keeper key set.
rationale: The PoC sends a cross-chain tx whose toContract is EthCrossChainData and whose method string 'f1121318093' hashes to the selector of putCurEpochConPubKeyBytes(bytes). The manager is EthCrossChainData's owner, so it passes onlyOwner and replaces the keeper key. The defect is in EthCrossChainManager (0x838bf9..., no recovered source): it lets any target and any method name build the call. EthCrossChainData and LockProxy have source but are only affected, and none of their Slither findings (e.g. arbitrary-send-eth in LockProxy) describe this flaw.

off_chain_reason: No realized loss: the PoC forks block 13038771 (~Aug 2021) and reproduces the msg.value-in-batch bug, which was found and rescued by a whitehat; the CSV loss field says all funds were returned.
violated_invariant: The ETH sent with a transaction (msg.value) must be credited once, not once per delegatecall inside batch().
rationale: The PoC calls DutchAuction.batch() with five copies of commitEth, so msg.value is counted five times because batch delegatecalls back into the contract. The real defect is msg.value reuse in the delegatecall batch loop (business logic), not missing input validation as the DHL label says. No source was recovered for the auction. I marked it out of scope as no real loss; the reviewer should check whether the 2021-09-16 date actually points to the separate MISO frontend supply-chain incident, which would also be out of scope.

violated_invariant: vVISR shares may only be minted for VISR the contract actually received.
rationale: RewardsHypervisor.deposit trusts a caller-supplied 'from' contract. It only checks IVisor(from).owner()==msg.sender, calls from.delegatedTransferERC20, and then mints shares without checking that its VISR balance went up. The PoC's contract returns itself as owner and has an empty delegatedTransferERC20, so it gets 1e26 shares for free. There is no reentrant call, so I think the DHL 'Reentrancy' label is wrong. Slither's arbitrary-send-erc20 (index 0) flags the other branch (safeTransferFrom with an arbitrary from), not the exploited path.

violated_invariant: ACOWriter must never make calls with its own identity to arbitrary targets, because users have given it standing ERC20 approvals.
rationale: write() takes a user-controlled exchangeAddress and exchangeData, and _sellACOTokens runs _exchange.call(exchangeData) without any allowlist. The PoC sets exchangeAddress=USDC and the data to transferFrom(victim 0xcb3203..., attacker, balance), which spends the victim's approval to ACOWriter. Its mock acoToken gets it past the earlier steps. Slither's low-level-calls (index 4) points at that exact line, but it is only an informational note about using a low-level call and does not describe the arbitrary-target weakness, so I left it out.

violated_invariant: An FNFT id's deposit-per-unit config must not change while that id is being minted, and getNextId() must account for an id mid-mint.
rationale: FNFTHandler.mint calls _mint, which triggers the onERC1155Received callback, before it increments fnftsCreated. In that callback the PoC reenters depositAdditionalToFNFT(fnftId,1e18,1). Its createNewSeries path uses getNextId(), which still equals the id being minted (360,000 units at depositAmount 0), so that id's per-unit value is raised to 1e18 and withdrawFNFT drains RENA. The flash swap only supplies working capital. Slither finding 46 (reentrancy-benign: FNFTHandler.mint writes fnftsCreated after the ERC1155 callback) describes exactly this ordering, though it rates it Low. FNFTHandler is a separately deployed contract whose address I have not verified, so it is not listed as a victim.

violated_invariant: Voting power used to pass and execute a proposal must not be acquirable and usable within a single transaction.
rationale: The PoC proposes a malicious BIP, warps one day, flash-borrows about $1B, deposits it into the Silo for instant Stalk, and calls emergencyCommit. The 2/3 supermajority is checked against power that counts immediately, and the BIP's init then drains the Silo. The defect is in GovernanceFacet behind the Diamond proxy (0xc1e088...). The recovered Diamond sources only contain the cut, loupe and ownership facets, so the defect code was not available to Slither, and no finding applies. The Bean token and Curve pools are only affected or used as tools.

violated_invariant: An account's borrow balance must be recorded before ETH is sent out, so collateral cannot be withdrawn while a borrow is outstanding.
rationale: borrowFresh calls doTransferOut (a raw ETH call in CEther) before it writes accountBorrows. The PoC's receive() reenters Comptroller.exitMarket, which has no reentrancy guard, sees zero debt, and frees the fUSDC collateral, which is then redeemed. The two victims are delegator/Unitroller proxies, and the defect lives in their CEtherDelegate and Comptroller implementations (sources included in the candidate's files). Slither finding 430 (reentrancy-no-eth on borrowFresh) flags accountBorrows written after external calls and readable cross-function through borrowBalanceStoredInternal. That is the exploited state, though it cites the comptroller calls rather than the ETH transfer, so treat it as borderline.

violated_invariant: Proxy-admin storage must not overlap the logic contract's Initializable flags, so initialize() stays one-shot behind the proxy.
rationale: AudiusAdminUpgradeabilityProxy declares proxyAdmin in slot 0. The pre-exploit logic (Staking.sol, DelegateManagerV2.sol) keeps Initializable's initialized/initializing bools in that same slot, so the admin address bytes make the initializer check pass again. The PoC re-initializes Governance, Staking and DelegateManager, delegates fake stake, then submits and executes a proposal that transfers AUDIO. Caution: the Governance logic candidate 0x1c91af... was deployed at block 15203848, after the fork block 15201793, and its Initializable already has the proxyAdmin fix. So it is the post-incident implementation, not the exploited code. Slither has no cross-contract storage-collision finding here.

violated_invariant: A DAO-module proposal must not execute Safe transactions unless the community has had a meaningful, bonded chance to dispute it.
rationale: Anyone can call addProposal. executeProposalWithIndex only needs the Reality.eth answer to be 1, a bond of at least minimumBond (0 disables the check), and the cooldown to have passed. The PoC answers its own question on Realitio, waits, then executes txs that mint 1e14 RNBW and hand PrimaryBridge/LPOP ownership to the attacker. This is a governance-design and configuration weakness (bond, cooldown, no monitoring or arbitrator), not a coding bug, and no Slither finding (event or timestamp notes) describes it. The realized USD loss looks small, so the reviewer may want to confirm in_scope.
